sources.title: Biran, Shenkar, Tabaldiev, Akmatov and Kolchenko, The Kök-Tash underground mausoleum
sources.note: Full original 2023 Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society archaeological article read. Qara Khitai identification is authors argued attribution, not certain. Use discussion footnotes 6, 80-81, chamber excavation and table reconstruction. Later adolescent burial and disturbed animal bones excluded.

sources.title: National Commission of the Kyrgyz Republic for UNESCO, Balasagun Town (Burana)
sources.note: Original national-commission site description, 2021. Not a UNESCO World Heritage statement. City spans 10th-14th centuries, minaret late 10th-early 11th, Qara Khitai capital 1130s-early13th. Avoid internally inconsistent height percentage and unverified legend.

sources.title: Coşkun Erdoğan, Women Rulers in the State of Qara Khitai
sources.note: Original 2024 article, Karadeniz Arastirmalari 21(81),156-176; full PDF read. Tabuyan printed162-164, Pusuwan164-167, marriage continuity169, English summary175-176. Do not extrapolate court patterns to all women.

sources.title: Michal Biran, Qarakhanid Studies: A View from the Qara Khitai Edge
sources.note: Original 2001 article, indexed PDF paragraphs13-16 read. Direct opens blocked by Anubis. Reproducible query: site.journals.openedition.org/asiecentrale/514 "Qara" "Bukhara". Supports trade and al-Faryabi moral book1200/bibliography, not universal schooling.

sources.title: Belyaev, Nastich and Sidorovich, The Coinage of Qara Khitay: A New Evidence
sources.note: Original university repository PDF read, printed130,136,138 and figures142-143. Coin legend 續興元寳, reading xu-xing yuan-bao. Article glosses 興 as thrive/prosper/flourish and 續 as continue; card gives short era-name translation Continued prosperity, not a claimed full literal translation of monetary formula. Yelu Yilie attribution is authors conclusion; find reports not sealed excavated contexts.

proposedOverrides.name: Qara Khitai (Western Liao)
proposedOverrides.summary: A Central Asian Khitan empire combining mobile rulers, established cities and subordinate states.

batchIdentityNotes.finding: One broad imported Central Asian outline, reaching far northwest into steppe beyond usual core geography; map start1200 and end1279 are coverage dates, not foundation/fall. History1124-1218, dynasty displaced1211; no alias with Liao, Qarakhanids or later Kirman dynasty. Public opening explicitly warns extent/date mismatch.
